files.content:
"use client";

import { AbsoluteCenter, Box, For, Text, VStack } from "@chakra-ui/react"

export const AbsoluteCenterWithAxis = () => {
  return (
    <VStack gap="6" align="stretch">
      <For each={["horizontal", "vertical", "both"]}>
        {(axis) => (
          <VStack gap="2" key={axis}>
            <Text fontWeight="medium">{`<AbsoluteCenter axis="${axis}" />`}</Text>
            <Box position="relative" h="80px" outline="1px solid red">
              <AbsoluteCenter axis={axis}>
                <Box
                  bg="blue.solid"
                  px="3"
                  py="1"
                  borderRadius="sm"
                  color="white"
                >
                  {axis}
                </Box>
              </AbsoluteCenter>
            </Box>
          </VStack>
        )}
      </For>
    </VStack>
  )
}

"use client";

import { AbsoluteCenter, Box } from "@chakra-ui/react"
import { LuHeart } from "react-icons/lu"

export const AbsoluteCenterWithContent = () => {
  return (
    <Box
      position="relative"
      w="100px"
      h="100px"
      bg="bg.muted"
      borderRadius="md"
    >
      <AbsoluteCenter>
        <Box
          bg="red.solid"
          color="white"
          p="3"
          borderRadius="full"
          fontSize="xl"
        >
          <LuHeart />
        </Box>
      </AbsoluteCenter>
    </Box>
  )
}

# Chakra UI absolute center

5 published Chakra UI absolute center examples with complete pinned source and MIT attribution.

## Installation

- Complete MIT examples with a ChakraProvider using defaultSystem.
- Reuse the application-level ChakraProvider when integrating; keep HiddenInput in checkbox and switch compositions for keyboard and form semantics.

- Copy every returned file and preserve the MIT licence notice.
- Render the returned preview.tsx example, or integrate the example into your existing provider.
